description: Coverage accounting. 'quarantine' lists tests that no CI leg executes, each with an owner, a review date and the gap it leaves; the Safety evidence job fails on any other never-executed test. 'dispositions' explain removed or weakened coverage; check_coverage_regression.py accepts only dispositions added by the same change. See docs/rules/safety-evidence.md.

quarantine.reason: Collation.Default snapshots the culture once per process, so the test passes only as the first LiteDB use in the process; after another test created a database it sees that culture instead of 'fi'.
quarantine.gap: A new database taking its collation from the current thread culture is not asserted on any CI leg; product behaviour (process-wide snapshot) decides whether the test can be made order-independent.

quarantine.reason: Not supported yet: rebuilding 'ana'/'ANA' from en-US/None to en-US/IgnoreCase throws 'Cannot insert duplicate key' instead of recording the collision in _rebuild_errors.
quarantine.gap: Rebuilding to a collation under which unique keys collide is not exercised; the expected _rebuild_errors behaviour is not implemented.

quarantine.reason: Takes ~102 s (100 iterations with a 1 s sleep; passed 5/5 locally on net10.0). The DiskWriterQueue race of #2127 no longer exists; the queue was removed in 198f0a672.
quarantine.gap: Back-to-back file-backed inserts into 100 recreated databases do not run in CI; the original race cannot recur, so the test is a candidate to retire as obsolete.

dispositions.invariant: Every test leg's results are uploaded and judged; no existing timeout, filter or partition changes.
dispositions.reason: Adds the Safety policy and Safety evidence jobs (10-minute limits) and a results upload for the .NET Framework leg, which uploaded nothing before; existing test steps keep their timeouts and filters.

dispositions.invariant: A real Windows sharing violation on the source during rebuild leaves the original data and WAL live and readable, with no temporary file.
dispositions.reason: Renamed and extended to both connection modes. Direct rebuild now claims the source exclusively before building, so an open foreign handle fails at source acquisition: the test asserts no live-state tag, no backup and no marker. The Shared variant still reaches the actual rename failure and keeps the old assertion (original-restored live state). Both variants now also assert byte-identical data and WAL, which the old test did not.

dispositions.invariant: Every existing test leg keeps its timeout, filter and partition; rebuild admission, ownership and rollback run on Linux, Windows and macOS for every PR.
dispositions.reason: Adds the rebuild-ownership job (20-minute limit): the RebuildOwnership*, RebuildAdmissionPlatform and Rebuild_InstallRollback classes on ubuntu, windows and macos, net8.0, in both tiers, so macOS file-lock semantics are checked on PRs although the ordinary macOS legs are full-tier only. The Safety evidence job requires it. The filter only selects an additional run; the ordinary legs still run these classes unfiltered.

dispositions.invariant: A file with damage found while opening is detected (INVALID_DATAFILE_STATE, or COLLATION_MISMATCH for a genuine ordering difference); an open that may not replace it leaves data and log byte-identical, and the first writable AutoRebuild open of a file recovers every document, keeps a backup equal to the source and reports the opening diagnostic.
dispositions.reason: #3051 slice S04 combines #3025 (explicit opening recovery, no rebuild mark from a refused open, read-only never replaces) and #3027 (recovery in the same open). The dev assertions that the first AutoRebuild open throws 999 and that a ReadOnly=true AutoRebuild open rebuilds are replaced: Issue2417 and Later_structural_corruption now first open without AutoRebuild (throws 999, bytes unchanged), then the first AutoRebuild open recovers with a byte-identical backup; Issue2417 asserts _rebuild_errors == 1 with stage=opening, pageType=Index and an int pageID (the #3027 value 0 came from a retry that dropped the opening cause). Requested_recovery drops ReadOnly=true from the rebuilding open and adds the negative case: a read-only AutoRebuild open is refused with COLLATION_MISMATCH, file unchanged, no backup. Issue2812CollationStamp additionally asserts the COLLATION_MISMATCH code with AutoRebuild=true. #3025 had no ledger entry for these changes.

dispositions.invariant: A default (non-AutoRebuild) open of a damaged 5.0.21 file reports the damaged collection and the remedies and changes nothing else; AutoRebuild recovers it once, in the open that found the damage, and a failure of that recovery keeps the damage that required it.
dispositions.reason: #3027 marked the file for rebuild (header byte 191) on the refused open and retried the open in the constructor (_markedForRebuild). DECISIONS D2 of #3051 adopts #3025's explicit opening recovery instead: a refused open writes nothing. The marking expectation (after[P_INVALID_DATAFILE_STATE] == 1, everything else equal) becomes the strictly stronger full byte equality in Default_open_reports_the_damage_and_leaves_the_file_unchanged (also repeated). The mark-write crash test (hook invalid-state-before-mark) is replaced by a bounded-attempt test: AutoRebuildAllowed is consulted exactly once and the rebuilt file is never rebuilt again. The caller-stream test asserts the stream bytes unchanged instead of a mark. The failed-retry tests are renamed Failed_opening_recovery_* and keep their exception assertions (the cause preservation is re-homed into the opening recovery) plus unchanged source bytes; the refused-admission test now asserts the unwrapped damage because a refusal is not a failed rebuild (only one exception exists).

dispositions.invariant: A failed rebuild-mark write during an error close does not trigger a second open or rebuild.
dispositions.reason: #3027 added this crash point inside MarkAsInvalidState for its mark-and-retry open. Under DECISIONS D2 an opening-validation refusal never reaches MarkAsInvalidState and there is no retry to suppress, so no test could hit the hook; it is not carried (MarkAsInvalidState stays void and unchanged, and S09 owns its rewritten body). Bounded opening recovery is covered by Auto_rebuild_runs_once_and_never_rebuilds_its_result_again and Failed_reopen_does_not_mark_candidate_invalid_or_create_another_backup.
